note: Angol tartalomréteg (gyakorlatok, tesztek, területek, rutinok, blokkok). A forrás a magyar adatfájl; azonosító szerint felülír, a számokat és a szerkezetet nem érinti.

push_wall.name: Wall push-up
push_wall.how: Stand an arm's length from the wall, hands at shoulder height, slightly wider than shoulder width. Lean towards the wall with a straight body until your nose almost touches it, then push yourself away.
points: One line from head to heels
Elbows at about 45 degrees, not out to the side

push_incline.name: Incline push-up on a table
push_incline.how: Put your hands on the edge of a sturdy table or counter. Lower your chest to the edge with a straight body, then push back. The lower the support, the harder it gets.
points: Abs and glutes tight, hips don't sag
Chest reaches first, not the chin

push_knee.name: Kneeling push-up
push_knee.how: In a kneeling plank with hands under the shoulders and the body straight from knees to head. Lower your chest to a few centimetres above the floor, then push up.
points: Hips in line with shoulders and knees
Elbows back, not out to the side
A brief pause at the bottom

push_full.name: Push-up
push_full.how: In a high plank with hands under the shoulders and the body straight from head to heels. Lower your chest to a fist's height, then push up to fully straight arms.
points: Elbows at about 45 degrees to the torso
At the top, push the shoulder blades apart too

push_decline.name: Decline push-up (feet raised)
push_decline.how: Feet on the edge of a chair or sofa, hands on the floor. Lower your chest with a straight body, then push up. A slow 3-second descent makes it even harder.
points: Straight torso, no arching of the lower back
Head in line with the spine

squat_box.name: Sit to stand from a chair
squat_box.how: Stand in front of a chair, feet hip-width apart. Starting with the hips going back, sit down until you touch, arms forward, then stand up without using your hands.
points: Knees point in the direction of the toes
Just touch the chair, don't drop onto it

squat.name: Squat
squat.how: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out. Squat down until your thighs are at least horizontal, chest up, then push up through your heels.

split_squat.name: Split squat
split_squat.how: Take a big step back with the back heel raised. Lower your back knee straight down to just above the floor, then push back up with the front leg. Do all reps on one side, then the other.
points: Back knee almost to the floor

bulgarian.name: Bulgarian split squat (back foot on a chair)
bulgarian.how: Back foot on a chair, the front foot about a big step in front. Lower yourself until the front thigh is horizontal, then push up through the front heel.

pistol_box.name: Single-leg squat to a chair
pistol_box.how: Standing on one leg in front of a chair, the other leg stretched forward. Slowly sit down until you touch, then stand up on the same leg. If it's easy, use a lower seat.
points: Knee towards the toes, not inwards

reverse_lunge.name: Reverse lunge
reverse_lunge.how: Take a big step back, lower your back knee to just above the floor, then push back to the start with the front leg. Alternate legs or do one side at a time.
points: Push back with the front leg

lateral_lunge.name: Side lunge
lateral_lunge.how: From a wide stance, sit onto one leg while the other stays straight, both soles on the floor. Push back to the middle.
points: The straight leg's sole stays down

tempo_lunge.name: Lunge with slow lowering
tempo_lunge.how: A reverse lunge, but lower yourself over 4 seconds, hold for 1 second at the bottom, then push up explosively.

glute_bridge.name: Glute bridge
glute_bridge.how: Lying on your back, knees bent, feet on the floor. Lift your hips until knees, hips and shoulders form a line, and squeeze your glutes for a moment at the top.
points: Push through the heels, not the toes
Don't arch your back at the top

sl_bridge.name: Single-leg glute bridge
sl_bridge.how: A glute bridge with one leg in the air, bent or straight. Keep the hips level throughout.
points: The pelvis doesn't tilt to the side
Hold for one second at the top

sl_hip_thrust.name: Single-leg hip thrust on a sofa
sl_hip_thrust.how: Shoulder blades on the edge of a sofa or sturdy chair, one foot on the floor. Lift your hips to horizontal, then lower to just above the floor.

prone_ytw.name: Prone Y–T–W raise
prone_ytw.how: Lying face down, forehead on the floor. Raise your arms in a Y shape, then a T shape, finally with bent elbows in a W shape, squeezing the shoulder blades each time. That is one rep.

snow_angel.name: Reverse snow angel (prone)
snow_angel.how: Lying face down, lift your chest and arms slightly off the floor. Sweep your arms in an arc from beside the hips to above your head and back, keeping them in the air.
points: Long neck, look at the floor

table_row_bent.name: Table row, knees bent
table_row_bent.how: Lie under a very stable, heavy table and grip the edge shoulder-width apart. Knees bent, feet on the floor: pull your chest up to the edge, then lower slowly. Check first that the table can't tip over.
points: Only with a completely stable table
Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top
Body straight from knees to head

table_row.name: Table row, legs straight
table_row.how: Like the previous one, but with straight legs and heels on the floor. The body stays a straight plank. Only with a stable table that can't tip over.

band_pull_apart.name: Band pull-apart
band_pull_apart.how: Hold the band shoulder-width apart, arms straight in front at shoulder height. Pull the band apart until it touches your chest, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Return slowly.
points: Shoulders stay down, not up to the ears

band_row.name: Band row
band_row.how: Anchor the band at waist height (with a door anchor or around a sturdy post). Step back so it's taut and pull your hands to your ribs, elbows going back. Return slowly.
points: Elbows travel back close to the body
Straight back, torso doesn't lean back
A brief squeeze at the end

band_row_single.name: Single-arm band row
band_row_single.how: Like the band row, but with one arm, in a split stance, with more tension. Don't let the torso rotate with the pull.

dead_hang.name: Dead hang on a bar
dead_hang.how: Grip the bar shoulder-width with an overhand grip and hang with straight arms. Finally pull the shoulder blades down a little (the body rises a few centimetres) and hold. If your feet touch the floor, bend your knees.
points: Only on a stable, securely mounted bar
Active shoulders, not hanging up to your ears

negative_pullup.name: Slow lowering (negative pull-up)
negative_pullup.how: Using a chair, step up so your chin is above the bar. From there, lower yourself over 4–5 seconds to straight arms. Step back on the chair and repeat.

chin_up.name: Chin-up
chin_up.how: Hang from the bar with an underhand grip, shoulder-width, and pull yourself up until your chin is above the bar. Lower slowly to straight arms. This is easier than the overhand grip.

pull_up.name: Pull-up
pull_up.how: Hang with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width and pull yourself up until your chin is above the bar. Lower slowly to straight arms.
points: Start by pulling the shoulder blades down

goblet_squat.name: Goblet squat
goblet_squat.how: Hold the weight in front of your chest with both hands (a kettlebell by the horns, a dumbbell by one end). Squat until your thighs are at least horizontal, elbows between the knees, then push up. Choose a weight with which the last 2 reps are hard but still clean. If it gets easy, increase the weight first, and only then switch to a harder exercise.
points: Knees in the direction of the toes

goblet_lunge.name: Reverse lunge with a weight
goblet_lunge.how: Holding the weight in front of your chest, step back, lower your back knee to just above the floor, then push back with the front leg. Choose a weight with which the last 2 reps are hard but still clean. If it gets easy, increase the weight first, and only then switch to a harder exercise.

goblet_bulgarian.name: Bulgarian split squat with a weight
goblet_bulgarian.how: Back foot on a chair, the weight in front of your chest. Lower yourself until the front thigh is horizontal, then push up through the front heel. Choose a weight with which the last 2 reps are hard but still clean. If it gets easy, increase the weight first, and only then switch to a harder exercise.

db_rdl.name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
db_rdl.how: Stand hip-width with the weight in front of your thighs. With slightly bent knees and a straight back, push your hips back and lower the weight to mid-shin, then stand up using your glutes. Choose a weight with which the last 2 reps are hard but still clean. If it gets easy, increase the weight first, and only then switch to a harder exercise.
points: The weight travels close to your legs
The hips go back; the back doesn't round

kb_swing.name: Kettlebell swing
kb_swing.how: In a wide stance, holding the weight with both hands, swing it back between your legs, then with a fast, powerful hip extension swing it forward to chest height. The arms only guide; the hips provide the momentum. It also works with a dumbbell held by one end. Choose a weight with which the last 2 reps are hard but still clean. If it gets easy, increase the weight first, and only then switch to a harder exercise.
points: From the hips, not a squat
Straight body at the top, glutes squeezed

sl_db_rdl.name: Single-leg dumbbell Romanian deadlift
sl_db_rdl.how: Standing on one leg with the weight in the opposite hand. Lean forward with a straight back as the free leg reaches back, then stand up. Choose a weight with which the last 2 reps are hard but still clean. If it gets easy, increase the weight first, and only then switch to a harder exercise.

db_row.name: Single-arm dumbbell row
db_row.how: Support yourself with one hand and knee on the edge of a chair or bench, back horizontal. With the other hand pull the weight towards your hip, elbow close to the body, then lower slowly. Choose a weight with which the last 2 reps are hard but still clean. If it gets easy, increase the weight first, and only then switch to a harder exercise.

db_row_pause.name: Dumbbell row with a pause at the top
db_row_pause.how: Like the single-arm row, but hold the weight at the top for 2 seconds with the shoulder blades squeezed, and lower it over 3 seconds. Choose a weight with which the last 2 reps are hard but still clean. If it gets easy, increase the weight first, and only then switch to a harder exercise.
points: Shoulder down, not at the ear

db_row_bent.name: Bent-over row with two dumbbells
db_row_bent.how: With slightly bent knees and a straight back, lean forward about 45 degrees, weights hanging. Pull both weights towards your hips together, then lower slowly. Choose a weight with which the last 2 reps are hard but still clean. If it gets easy, increase the weight first, and only then switch to a harder exercise.
points: Elbows back, close to the body

dead_bug.name: Dead bug
dead_bug.how: Lying on your back, arms up, knees and hips at 90 degrees. Slowly extend the opposite arm and leg to just above the floor while your lower back stays on the floor. Return, then the other side.
points: Lower back pressed to the floor throughout
Only extend as far as the lower back stays down

plank.name: Forearm plank
plank.how: On your forearms with elbows under the shoulders, body straight from head to heels. Brace your abs and glutes and hold.
points: Stop if your lower back starts to shake

plank_taps.name: Plank shoulder taps
plank_taps.how: In a high plank with feet a little wider, tap the opposite shoulder with alternating hands without letting the hips rock.

hollow.name: Hollow body hold
hollow.how: Lying on your back, lift your shoulders and straight legs off the floor, arms beside your head. Keep your lower back on the floor. Easier: knees bent, arms by your sides.
points: If the lower back lifts, raise your legs higher

side_plank_knee.name: Kneeling side plank
side_plank_knee.how: Lying on your side, prop yourself on your forearm with knees bent. Lift your hips so knees, hips and shoulders form a line, and hold.

side_plank.name: Side plank
side_plank.how: Lying on your side on your forearm with straight legs, feet stacked. Lift your hips to a straight body and hold.
points: Body straight from head to heels
Top arm on the hip or in the air

side_plank_lift.name: Side plank with leg lift
side_plank_lift.how: In a side plank, slowly lift the top leg and lower it again while the hips stay up.

speed_squat.name: Fast squat to toes
speed_squat.how: Squat halfway down, then stand up onto your toes as fast as you can with an arm swing. No jumping; gentle on the knees.

squat_jump.name: Squat jump
squat_jump.how: Squat halfway down and jump as high as you can. Land softly with bent knees, straight into the next squat.

broad_jump_rep.name: Standing broad jump
broad_jump_rep.how: With an arm swing, jump forward as far as you can and land stably on both feet with bent knees. Walk back; that's the rest.

skater.name: Skater hops
skater.how: Jump sideways from one leg to the other and land on one leg, as if skating. Gradually increase the distance.
points: Land on one leg and hold

tuck_jump.name: Tuck jump
tuck_jump.how: Jump up from standing and pull your knees towards your chest in the air. Soft landing, a short pause, then the next.
points: A high jump, not a fast series

fast_feet.name: Fast feet on the spot
fast_feet.how: With slightly bent knees, on your toes, tap on the spot as fast as you can, feet barely leaving the floor.

high_knees.name: High knees on the spot
high_knees.how: Run on the spot, raising your knees to hip height with fast arm work. Short, all-out bursts.

mountain_climber.name: Mountain climber
mountain_climber.how: In a high plank, drive your knees alternately towards your chest at a fast pace. Keep your hips at shoulder and heel height.

burpee.name: Burpee
burpee.how: Squat, hands to the floor, feet back into a plank, feet back in, stand up and do a small jump. In a steady, continuous rhythm.
points: Better slower but with good technique

sl_stand.name: Single-leg stand
sl_stand.how: Stand on one leg with the other knee slightly raised. Look at one point. If it's easy, slowly turn your head left and right.
points: Touch the wall with a fingertip if needed

sl_stand_closed.name: Single-leg stand, eyes closed
sl_stand_closed.how: A single-leg stand, but with your eyes closed. Stand close to a wall or the back of a chair so you can hold on.
points: A safe spot with something to hold

sl_reach.name: Single-leg forward reach
sl_reach.how: Standing on one leg, lean forward with a straight back as the free leg reaches back and your hand reaches towards the floor. Return slowly.

warmup.name: Warm-up
warmup.how: March on the spot with high knees, arm circles forwards and backwards, hip circles, 10 easy squats, 10 alternating lunges. Get warm by the end, but don't get tired.
points: Slightly faster breathing at the end

breathing.name: Slow breathing
breathing.how: Lie on your back or sit comfortably. Breathe in through your nose for 4 seconds, hold for 4, breathe out over 6 seconds. Make the exhale longer than the inhale: it helps you calm down after training.
points: If you feel dizzy, breathe normally

cat_cow.name: Cat–cow
cat_cow.how: On all fours, as you breathe in let your belly drop and lift your head; as you breathe out round your back, chin towards your chest. One vertebra at a time.
points: Slow, in time with the breath

worlds_greatest.name: Lunge with elbow to instep and rotation
worlds_greatest.how: A big forward lunge, back knee down or up. Bring the elbow on the same side as the front leg towards the inside of the ankle, then reach the same arm to the ceiling, rotating the torso. Finally straighten the front leg, hips back.
points: Follow your hand with your eyes when rotating

open_book.name: Open book (thoracic rotation)
open_book.how: Lying on your side, knees bent, arms stretched forward on top of each other. Sweep the top arm in an arc to the other side, eyes following, knees staying put. Return.

wall_slide.name: Wall slide
wall_slide.how: Back against the wall, with lower back, back and head on the wall. Arms in a W shape against the wall: slide them up to a Y while arms and hands stay on the wall, then back.
points: Lower back doesn't arch away from the wall
Elbows and wrists on the wall
Only as far as the arms stay on the wall

towel_dislocate.name: Shoulder pass-through with a towel
towel_dislocate.how: Hold a long towel with a wide grip. With straight arms, take it over your head to behind you, then back to the front. If it's hard, grip wider.

squat_hold.name: Deep squat hold
squat_hold.how: Squat as deep as you can with heels on the floor. Push your knees out with your elbows, chest up. If your heels lift, hold on to a door frame.
points: Knees in the direction of the toes

ankle_rock.name: Knee to wall (ankle mobility)
ankle_rock.how: In a split stance facing the wall, front toes 5–10 cm from the wall. The heel stays down; push the knee forward towards the wall, then back.

hip_9090.name: 90/90 hip switch
hip_9090.how: Sit with both knees at 90 degrees, one leg in front of you, the other to the side. Slowly rotate your knees to the other side with a straight back. If it's hard, support yourself with your hands behind you.

couch_stretch.name: Hip flexor stretch
couch_stretch.how: In a half-kneeling position (cushion under the knee), push forward with your hips and squeeze the glute on the back-leg side. Feel the stretch at the front of the thigh.

hamstring_stretch.name: Hamstring stretch
hamstring_stretch.how: Lying on your back, lift one straight leg and hold it behind the thigh (or with a towel around the foot). Pull it towards you until you feel a pleasant stretch.
points: Other leg straight on the floor

glute_stretch.name: Glute stretch (figure four)
glute_stretch.how: Lying on your back, put one ankle on the other thigh and pull your legs towards your chest. You feel it on the outer side of the glute.

calf_stretch.name: Calf stretch at the wall
calf_stretch.how: In a split stance, lean on the wall with the back leg straight and the heel on the floor. Push your hips forward.

child_pose.name: Child's pose with breathing
child_pose.how: From kneeling, sit back on your heels and stretch your arms forward on the floor, forehead down. Breathe deeply into your back.

mobility.name: Mobility
mobility.about: How large a range your joints move through under control: squat, shoulder, ankle.

flexibility.name: Flexibility
flexibility.about: How stretchable your muscles are: hamstrings, hip flexors.

strength.name: Strength
strength.about: Upper body and legs, with your own body weight.

core.name: Core endurance
core.about: How long you can hold your torso stable: this protects your lower back.

power.name: Speed and power
power.about: How much force you can produce quickly: jumping, changing direction.

balance.name: Balance and coordination
balance.about: On one leg, with eyes closed, and down to the floor and up.

cardio.name: Endurance
cardio.about: The capacity of your heart and lungs. Your fitness age comes from this.

deep_squat.name: Deep squat
deep_squat.how: Barefoot, feet hip-width apart, arms stretched overhead. Squat as deep as you can and hold for 3 seconds. Ask someone to watch from the side, or check yourself in a mirror.
options: Thighs below horizontal, heels down, torso roughly upright, arms stay up
I get down, but my heels lift or my torso leans far forward
My thighs don't even reach horizontal
I feel pain while doing it

shoulder_reach.name: Hands meeting behind the back
shoulder_reach.how: Standing, bring one hand from above and the other from below behind your back and try to bring your fists towards each other in one movement. Measure the distance between the fists relative to your hand length (wrist to the tip of the middle finger). Do it the other way too, and enter the worse side.
options: Between one and one and a half hand lengths
Further than one and a half hand lengths
I feel pain while doing it

ankle_wall.name: Knee to wall (ankle)
ankle_wall.how: Stand in a split stance facing the wall, front toes towards the wall. Keep your heel down and push your knee to the wall. Find the largest toe–wall distance from which the knee can still just touch the wall. Measure both sides and enter the worse one.

sit_reach.name: Sit and reach
sit_reach.how: Sit on the floor with straight legs, soles against a wall or box. After warming up, slowly reach forward with one hand on top of the other as far as you can and hold for 2 seconds. Measure how many centimetres you reached past your toes (positive number) or how many were missing (negative number). Best of two attempts.

hip_flexor.name: Hip flexor test on the edge of a bed
hip_flexor.how: Sit on the edge of a bed and lie back while pulling one knee to your chest. The other leg hangs loosely off the bed. Look (or ask someone) where the hanging thigh is. Both sides; enter the worse one.
options: The thigh lies on the bed or below it, the knee bends to about a right angle
The thigh is on the bed, but the knee straightens and doesn't bend to a right angle
The thigh rises above the level of the bed
I feel pain while doing it

pushup.name: Push-ups to fatigue
pushup.how: Men do full push-ups, women kneeling push-ups (this is how the CSEP norm measures). Chest down to a fist's height, up to fully straight arms, with a straight body. Keep going without stopping as long as your technique holds. The last, incomplete rep doesn't count.
pushup.safety: Skip it if your shoulder or wrist hurts.

chair_stand.name: 30-second chair stand
chair_stand.how: Sit on a chair about 43–45 cm high, placed against a wall, arms crossed over your chest. On the signal, for 30 seconds stand up fully and sit back down as fast as you safely can. Count the full stands.

plank.name: Forearm plank to fatigue
plank.how: On your forearms with elbows under the shoulders, body straight from head to heels. Start the stopwatch and hold as long as your body stays straight. Stop as soon as your hips drop or rise.
plank.safety: Stop immediately if your lower back hurts.

broad_jump.name: Standing broad jump
broad_jump.how: After warming up, stand behind a line and with an arm swing jump forward from two feet to two feet. Measure from the line to your back heel. Jump three times and enter the best. On a non-slip surface.
broad_jump.safety: Skip it if your knee, ankle or lower back hurts.

tapping.name: 15-second fast feet
tapping.how: On your toes, tap on the spot as fast as you can for 15 seconds and count the floor contacts of your right foot (or record a video and count afterwards). There is no age norm for this: it measures your own progress.

reaction.name: Reaction time
reaction.how: Hold the phone comfortably in your hand. When the field changes colour, tap it as fast as you can. There are five trials; if you tap too early, that trial doesn't count. The measured time includes the phone's latency, so always measure on the same phone and only look at your own progress.

vertical_jump.name: Vertical jump height
vertical_jump.how: Prop the phone up to the side, about 2–3 metres away, so your whole body is visible. Stand upright, then with an arm swing jump as high as you can from standing and land softly. Jump three times with a few seconds' pause; the best jump counts. The camera estimates from the time spent in the air; accuracy has not yet been validated on real recordings. Check the result and correct it if needed. Without a camera: stand next to a wall, mark the highest point with your arm stretched, then again when jumping, and enter the difference.
vertical_jump.safety: Skip it if your knee, ankle or lower back hurts.

sl_stance.name: Single-leg stance with eyes closed
sl_stance.how: Barefoot, hands on hips, stand on one leg, lift the other and close your eyes. Time stops when you open your eyes, put your foot down or your sole moves. Measure both the right and the left leg and enter the average. Stand close to a wall.

sway.name: Balance with the accelerometer
sway.how: Press the phone to your chest with both hands, stand on one leg and look at one point. For 20 seconds I measure your sway with the phone's motion sensor. 100 is completely still; the higher, the more stable. Stand close to a wall.

tug.name: Timed up and go (TUG)
tug.how: Sit on a chair with armrests, back against the backrest. On the signal, stand up, walk at your usual pace to a mark 3 metres away, turn around, walk back and sit down. Measure the time from starting to sitting back down. Above 12 seconds it's worth talking to a doctor or physiotherapist about fall prevention.
tug.safety: Only if you can walk safely; if you use a walking stick, do it with the stick.

sit_rise.name: Sit down on the floor and stand up
sit_rise.how: Barefoot and standing, without using your hands or knees, sit down cross-legged, then stand up the same way. You start from 10 points and lose a point for every support you use with a hand, forearm, knee or the side of your leg (one point per support, both when sitting down and standing up), plus half a point if you lose balance. Enter the final score (0–10).

step_test.name: 3-minute step test
step_test.how: You need a step or stable stool about 30 cm high. To the beat of the metronome (96 beats per minute, i.e. 24 full step-ups) step up-up-down-down for 3 minutes. Then sit down immediately and count your heartbeats at your wrist over the next full 60 seconds. Enter the total number of beats counted. A watch's momentary heart rate shown at the end of a minute is a different measurement and can't be used for this norm. If you measured that way before, repeat the test with this method.
step_test.safety: Stop immediately if you feel dizzy, have chest pain or very strong shortness of breath. With heart disease or blood pressure medication (beta blockers) this test does not give a reliable result.

vitals.how: For your fitness age: resting heart rate (in the morning before getting up, or after 5 minutes of sitting calmly), waist (at navel height, at the end of an exhale) and three questions about your weekly activity.
frequency: Never, or less than once a week
intensity: Easily, I don't sweat or get out of breath
I get out of breath and sweat
I push myself to near exhaustion

morning.name: Morning wake-up
morning.about: Loosening up after waking: spine, hips, shoulders.

office.name: Office mobility
office.about: After a lot of sitting: thoracic rotation, hip flexors, shoulders. Can also be done at a chair.

evening.name: Evening stretch
evening.about: Slow stretching and breathing before bed, to help you fall asleep.

ski.name: Pre-ski preparation
ski.about: Leg strength, lateral stability and balance before the season. The detailed version personalised with a movement assessment is in Kanyar.

core.name: Core strength
core.about: Front and side core, glutes: the basis of the pre-beach-season block.

runner.name: For runners
runner.about: Ankle, calf and glutes: preventing the most common running injuries (knee, Achilles).

cyclist.name: For cyclists
cyclist.about: Counterbalancing the forward-leaning position: hip flexors, thoracic spine, glutes and core.

tennis.name: For tennis players
tennis.about: Lateral movement, trunk rotation and shoulder stability.

football.name: For footballers
football.about: Knee and ankle stability, hamstrings and groin: preventing common football injuries.

balance60.name: Balance over 60
balance60.about: Safe balance and strength exercises with something to hold on to (chair, wall).

ski.name: Pre-ski preparation
ski.about: In autumn, before the season: leg strength, lateral stability, balance.

summer_run.name: Summer running season
summer_run.about: In spring: injury prevention alongside running (best together with the running programme).

beach.name: Core before beach season
beach.about: In early summer: core and glutes with short, intense sessions.

captions.Alsó fogás · áll a rúd fölé: Underhand grip · chin over the bar
captions.Boka a térden, combot a mellkas felé: Ankle on knee, thigh towards the chest
captions.Csípő a sarok felé, karok előre nyújtva: Hips towards the heels, arms stretched forward
captions.Csípő fent, a derék nem homorít: Hips up, lower back not arched
captions.Csípő hátra, súly a lábak között: Hips back, weight between the legs
captions.Egy lábon, csípőre tett kézzel: On one leg, hands on hips
captions.Egyik kéz és térd a padon: One hand and knee on the bench
captions.Felső fogás · áll a rúd fölé: Overhand grip · chin over the bar
captions.Felső kar a másik oldalra, térdek együtt: Top arm to the other side, knees together
captions.Felülnézet · oldalt fekve, térdek egymás: Top view · lying on the side, knees stacked
captions.Fent 2 mp tartás, majd 3 mp leengedés: Hold 2 s at the top, then lower over 3 s
captions.Fent · stabil asztalon támaszkodva: Up · leaning on a stable table
captions.Hátsó láb stabil széken: Back foot on a stable chair
captions.Kar csúszik felfelé Y alakba: Arms slide up into a Y
captions.Kar nyújtva · csak stabil asztal alatt: Arms straight · only under a stable table
captions.Karnyújtásnyira a faltól: An arm's length from the wall
